note: The coding lane model-facing contract: wire names, descriptions with rendered examples, flat git tools. The native binding lane is asserted against this fixture byte-for-byte (modulo the host DirectWrite annotation prefix). The 2026-11-02 TypeScript-pack freeze (canonical ids, git_inspect) is superseded because the model now sees the dialect's names; regenerate it deliberately when the dialect table or a description changes.

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text in an existing file: old_string becomes new_string, once per call. old_string must match exactly one place in the file (whitespace and quotes are matched leniently only when no exact match exists); keep it as small as possible while unique, or set replace_all to change every occurrence. Line endings and any BOM are preserved, and the call is refused with file_changed if the file changed since you last read it. Read the file first. Returns a unified diff and the new sha256.

Example: edit({"file_path":"src/lib.rs","old_string":"let retries = 3;","new_string":"let retries = 5;"})
Example: edit({"file_path":"src/lib.rs","old_string":"old_name","new_string":"new_name","replace_all":true})

file_path.description: File to edit, relative to the workspace root.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace; it must match one place in the file.

new_string.description: Replacement text. An empty string deletes the matched text.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match. Default false.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description:
Show changes (read-only): the unstaged working tree changes, or the staged changes with staged true; rev compares against a commit, branch, tag or range, and path limits the diff to one file or directory. Use it instead of running git through run_shell_command. Repository hooks, fsmonitor, filter, textconv and external-diff drivers, the pager and ssh helpers are neutralized and never run; paths are taken literally; output is capped.

Example: git_diff({"path":"src/lib.rs","staged":true})

path.description: Limit to this path (relative to the workspace root). Taken literally: no globs or pathspec magic.

rev.description: Commit, branch, tag or range, e.g. HEAD~2.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description:
List commits, newest first (read-only). limit sets how many (default 20); rev starts from a commit, branch or tag; path keeps only commits that touch it. Use it instead of running git through run_shell_command. Repository hooks, fsmonitor, filter, textconv and external-diff drivers, the pager and ssh helpers are neutralized and never run; paths are taken literally; output is capped.

Example: git_log({"limit":10})

path.description: Limit to this path (relative to the workspace root). Taken literally: no globs or pathspec magic.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits (command log only).

rev.description: Commit, branch, tag or range, e.g. HEAD~2.

tools.name: git_show
tools.description: Show one commit with its changes (read-only). rev names the commit, branch or tag (default HEAD), for example HEAD~2; path limits the output to one file or directory. Use it instead of running git through run_shell_command. Repository hooks, fsmonitor, filter, textconv and external-diff drivers, the pager and ssh helpers are neutralized and never run; paths are taken literally; output is capped.

path.description: Limit to this path (relative to the workspace root). Taken literally: no globs or pathspec magic.

rev.description: Commit, branch, tag or range, e.g. HEAD~2.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description:
Show the working tree status and the current branch (read-only). Use it instead of running git through run_shell_command. path limits the report to one file or directory. Repository hooks, fsmonitor, filter, textconv and external-diff drivers, the pager and ssh helpers are neutralized and never run; paths are taken literally; output is capped.

Example: git_status({})

path.description: Limit to this path (relative to the workspace root). Taken literally: no globs or pathspec magic.

tools.name: glob
tools.description:
Find files by name with a glob such as **/*.ts or src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}. Use it to locate a file; to search inside files use grep_search, to see one folder use list_directory. Respects .gitignore, .ignore and .git/info/exclude; skips .git, node_modules, symlinks and credential files. Returns up to 1000 paths, one per line. Use this instead of grep, rg, find or ls in a shell command.

Example: glob({"pattern":"**/*.rs"})
Example: glob({"pattern":"*.test.ts","path":"src","limit":20})

pattern.description: Glob matched against paths relative to the search directory, or against the file name.

path.description: Directory to search. Default: the workspace root.

limit.description: Maximum number of paths to return.

tools.name: grep_search
tools.description:
Search the text of workspace files for a regular expression. Output lines are "<path>:<line>:<text>". Use it to find where something is defined or used; to find a file by name use glob. Respects .gitignore, .ignore and .git/info/exclude; skips .git, node_modules, symlinks, binary and credential files. Bounded: 10000 entries, 1 MiB per file, 48 KiB output, 20s; a bounded search says so. Use this instead of grep, rg, find or ls in a shell command.

Example: grep_search({"pattern":"fn main"})
Example: grep_search({"pattern":"TODO|FIXME","path":"src","glob":"*.rs","limit":20})

pattern.description: Regular expression. Escape special characters with a backslash to match them literally.

path.description: File or directory. Default: the workspace root.

glob.description: Only files matching this glob, such as *.ts.

tools.name: list_directory
tools.description:
List the entries of one directory in the workspace; directories end with /, symlinks with @. Use it to see what a folder holds, glob to search by name and repo_map for an overview of the whole project. Shows at most 500 entries; credential files and entries matched by .gitignore are hidden unless include_ignored is true. Prefer the native tools (read_file, list_directory, glob, grep_search, repo_map) over shell commands for exploring code.

Example: list_directory({})
Example: list_directory({"path":"src","include_ignored":true})

path.description: Directory, relative to the workspace root. Default: the root.

include_ignored.description: Also list entries matched by .gitignore, .ignore and .git/info/exclude.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description:
Read one text file in the workspace and return its lines numbered "<n>\t<line>". Use it before edit or write_file; to locate code first use grep_search or glob. Returns at most 2000 lines or 50.0KB per call and ends with a continuation notice (offset=N) when more remains; offset is 1-based. A file unchanged since an earlier read in this chat whose result is still in context returns the one-line stub "[unchanged since call <id> ...]" instead of its text; pass force=true to get the text. Read several files with several calls. Prefer the native tools (read_file, list_directory, glob, grep_search, repo_map) over shell commands for exploring code.

Example: read_file({"file_path":"src/main.rs"})
Example: read_file({"file_path":"src/main.rs","offset":120,"limit":80})

file_path.description: File to read, relative to the workspace root.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return.

force.description: Return the text even when the file is unchanged since an earlier read still in context. Default false.

tools.name: repo_map
tools.description:
Orient yourself in a repository: top-level manifests (package.json, tsconfig, Cargo.toml, pyproject, go.mod, README) with short excerpts, plus a depth-limited directory tree (default depth 3, max 400 entries). Respects ignore files. Call this first in an unfamiliar project, before any shell command; to look inside one folder use list_directory.

Example: repo_map({})
Example: repo_map({"path":"crates","depth":2})

depth.description: How many directory levels the tree shows.

tools.name: run_shell_command
tools.description:
Run a shell command (bash -c) in the workspace WITHOUT a sandbox. Use it for builds, tests and tooling. Do NOT use it to read or search files, list directories or inspect git: use read_file, list_directory, glob, grep_search, repo_map and git_status, git_diff, git_log or git_show, which are cheaper and safer. Output keeps the last 2000 lines / 50 KB. Default timeout 120s, max 600s; timeout is in milliseconds.

Example: run_shell_command({"command":"cargo build --workspace"})
Example: run_shell_command({"command":"npm run lint","directory":"web","timeout":120000})

directory.description: Directory inside the workspace. Default: the root.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description:
Run one of the project's configured test commands, exactly as written: "bun test". Use it to check your change; for any other command use run_shell_command. Same sandbox and output limits as run_shell_command, and the run is limited to 600s. The result is the command's output tail and exit status.

Example: run_tests({"command":"bun test"})

command.description: One of the allowed test commands, verbatim.

tools.name: submit_plan
tools.description:
Propose a plan for the user to approve. Only meaningful in plan mode: there it is the ONLY way to be granted write and command execution — the call pauses for the user, and if they approve, this call completes and you may edit and run commands as the granted mode allows. Write the plan so a person can decide from it alone: which files change, in what order, how each change is verified.

Example: submit_plan({"plan":"1. Add the retry limit to src/client.rs.\n2. Cover it in tests/client.rs.\n3. Verify with the configured test command.","mode":"auto_edit"})

plan.description: The plan, in markdown. What changes and how it is verified.

mode.description: The permission mode you are asking for. Advisory: the host decides what it grants, and a reviewer/supervisor role ceiling still applies.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description:
Create a text file or replace the whole content of an existing one inside the workspace; parent directories are created, .git is refused, and content is at most 5.0MB. Overwriting a file requires that you read it completely in this session first, and is refused with file_changed if the file changed since. To change part of a file use edit instead. Returns the new sha256.

Example: write_file({"file_path":"docs/notes.md","content":"# Notes

First line.
"})

file_path.description: File to write, relative to the workspace root.
